key_insight: The paper shows that nonlinear dynamics can be simulated on near-term quantum hardware by learning a finite-dimensional Koopman linear representation and evolving it with shallow quantum circuits.
engineering_relevance: It provides a practical path for quantum simulation of real-world multiscale systems where direct unitary encoding of nonlinear evolution is otherwise infeasible.
method: Learn Koopman observables from trajectory data
Project the lifted nonlinear dynamics into a finite-dimensional linear subspace
Decompose the non-unitary propagator into parallel spectral channels for quantum execution
evidence_signal: The method was validated on a superconducting processor across three nonlinear systems, using up to 32 parallel 10-qubit circuits and reproducing dominant patterns and statistical signatures.
watch_item: Performance depends on the balance between hardware noise and the accuracy limits of the finite Koopman approximation, so strongly nonlinear systems may remain representation-limited.
paper_title: Quantum simulation of real-world nonlinear dynamics via Koopman method
